conviction_note: Funko beat its own quarterly sales guide by about 5-7 points in both Q1 and Q2 2026, and the stock was bought each time (+17.9%, +11.4%). Q3 consensus (~$250.7M) sits exactly on the 'approximately flat' guide. Toy peers that reported after Funko last spoke were strong (JAKKS +20%, Hasbro raised its FY guide), 7.6M shares are short (7.6 days to cover), and an activist holds about 23% economic exposure. That gives p_up 60 on a 15-point absolute move (+3.0). Two things hold it there: management's stated caution on the Q4 consumer, and a Pop Mart Americas collapse that reads ambiguously for collectibles. The findings sum to +5.1, which is larger than the scaled +3.0; most of that sum is the guide-beat pattern, which a cautious Q4 guide can override.
bar: Q3 2026 net sales 'approximately flat' YoY on Q3 2025's $250.9M, i.e. ~$250.9M; gross margin ~43-44%; adj. EBITDA $25-30M (company guide, 2026-08-06, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001704711/000170471126000044/ex-9918626.htm). Estimates agree: revenue $250.70M (MarketBeat), $249.6M (Benzinga), $252M (Earnings Whispers), EPS $0.09-0.10. FY26 guide: net sales flat to +3% ($908-935M) against an FY consensus of ~$927.8M; adj. EBITDA $100-110M including the $25.4M Q2 tariff benefit. Bar is sourced to the company guide plus agreeing estimates, so sizes are not capped.
positioning_check: Short interest 7.6M shares, 7.6 days to cover, at the 2026-09-30 settlement, up from 6.7M and 5.2 days at 2026-09-15 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/fnko/short-interest/; the fetch returned 403, so this is snippet_only from search). That is about 13.6% of the 55.996M shares outstanding. Fintel shows 12.5% of float, undated (https://fintel.io/ss/us/fnko). Activist Fund 1 Investments (Pleasant Lake) holds 9.9% plus cash-settled swaps on 13.0%, about 23% economic exposure (13D/A No.5, event 2026-10-14). No skew: the option chain is unusable (not two-sided); put/call OI 0.77 on 1,159 contracts. Unusual Whales quotes an implied ±26.8% that could not be verified. Tape: spot $6.11, -8.7% over 5 days, -6.0% over 20 days, about -10.5% from the ~$6.83 print of 2026-10-15, +117% off the 52-week low.

findings.finding: Funko has guided low and beaten its own quarterly sales guide twice in 2026, and Q3 consensus sits exactly on the new low guide. Q1: guided flat to -2%, printed +5.3%. Q2: guided +1% to +6%, printed +7.4% ($207.7M); Q2 adj. EBITDA excluding the $25.4M tariff benefit was ~$15.5M against a $5-10M guide. Q3 is guided 'approximately flat' (~$250.9M) with adj. EBITDA $25-30M, and consensus is $249.6-252M, i.e. on the guide with no beat built in.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 sales beat of the guide: +17.94%. Q2 2026 beat above the high end, with the EBITDA guide raised: +11.36%. Q3 2025 sales slightly below estimates: still +10.26%. In 2025 guide misses and cuts brought -13.55%, -16.43% and -32.79%.
findings.why_not_priced: Estimates sit on the guide midpoint ($250.7M vs $250.9M), so the sell-side has not modelled a third beat. If a beat were priced, consensus would sit above the flat guide, and the stock would not be -10% since mid-October into the print.
findings.independence: Q1 actual vs guide comes from a separate primary document, the Q1 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001704711/000170471126000034/ex-9915726.htm). Peer prints (finding 2) point the same way from different sources.

findings.finding: Toy peers that reported after Funko's last call (2026-08-06) had a strong Q3, especially in licensed lines. JAKKS Q3 net sales +20% to $254.2M, North America +28% (10-Q 2026-10-27). Hasbro Q3 revenue +15%, Consumer Products +4% with Marvel +35% on Spider-Man: Brand New Day and KPop Demon Hunters, FY guide raised to +7-9% (2026-10-20). Circana US toy dollars were +17% in H1 2026, licensed +24%. This is a proxy; Funko's own Q2 POS was only +6% in units.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline row isolates peer read-through. Funko's Q2 2026 call cited POS momentum 'across theatrical, anime, gaming and sports' and the print was +11.36%.
findings.why_not_priced: Funko's Q3 consensus has not moved off the flat guide since the peer prints. If the read-through were priced, estimates would sit above $251M and FNKO would not have fallen ~10% since mid-October while peers reported well.
findings.independence: JAKKS Q3 2026 (https://finviz.com/news/406783/jakks-pacific-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results, 10-Q 2026-10-27) and Circana H1 2026 (https://www.licenseglobal.com/toys-games/u-s-toy-industry-achieves-strongest-first-half-growth-in-six-years-circana) are separate sources. Funko's own Q2 POS (+6% units, US mid-single digits, Europe +20%) shows Funko lagging the category; that is why this is sized small.

findings.finding: The FY26 net sales guide (flat to +3%, reiterated 2026-08-06) implies Q4 of -9% to +1% YoY. H1 was +6.3% ($408.6M vs $384.2M) and Q3 is guided flat, so a Q3 at or above guide mechanically lifts the low end. The FY consensus (~$927.8M, +2.2%) already sits in the upper half, so a raise only to the consensus is roughly neutral, and holding the range would read as a Q4 cut.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 EBITDA guide raise: +11.36%. March 2026 first FY guide (flat to +3%): -3.95%. 2025 guide withdrawal and cut: -16.43% and -32.79%.
findings.why_not_priced: The guide still tells the market Q4 could fall up to 9%. A raise would be news against the printed range, though less so against the consensus. Management said on the Q2 call it 'will continue to be prudent' and that Q4 visibility is lower (https://www.webull.com/news/15398317687907328), so a hold is possible. This is why the range is wide.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2 release with finding 1 but rests on a different line (the FY guide arithmetic, not Q3 vs guide). Hasbro's raised FY guide and 'strong finish to 2026' comment is separate support.

findings.finding: The Q2 10-Q says that if the refinancing plans are not completed before the end of fiscal 2026, the $201M of debt reclassifies to a current liability. The Q3 release and 10-Q are the last update before that date. The net leverage covenant (max 2.50x) is waived for 2026-09-30 and first tested at 2026-12-31. Answering the financing question: the company is not funding a ramp. It is refinancing a facility it has already paid down by $24M in H1. With FY adj. EBITDA guided at $100-110M (about $75-85M excluding the one-off), net leverage is roughly 2x, which should make an extension or refinancing obtainable.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The February 2026 maturity extension (8-K 2026-02-13) was not on a print day. In 2025, prints that carried refinancing and going-concern anxiety fell (-16.43%, -32.79%), but they also carried guide cuts.
findings.why_not_priced: The deadline sits in a 10-Q footnote, not in the preview copy. If it were priced either way, there would be either a distress discount (the stock is +117% off its low) or a takeover premium, and neither is visible.
findings.independence: The 8-K of 2026-02-13 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1704711/000170471126000005/fnko-20260213.htm) sets the December 2027 maturity and the covenant schedule. Same issuer, different document.

findings.finding: Activist Fund 1 Investments (Pleasant Lake), which publicly pushed Funko toward a sale in February 2026, raised its cash-settled swap exposure from 9.4% of shares (13D/A No.3, event 2026-06-12) to 13.0% (13D/A No.5, event 2026-10-14). It also holds 9.9% in stock, so its economic exposure is about 23% going into the print. Funko's own 10-Q still says the board will evaluate strategic alternatives 'with the assistance of financial advisors'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print has carried a strategic-transaction update. The February 2026 activist disclosure was off-cycle.
findings.why_not_priced: The amendment was filed on 2026-10-16 with no Item 4 change and drew no coverage, and the stock has fallen ~10% since. If a takeover floor were priced, the stock would not be sliding into the print alongside a rising activist stake.
findings.independence: The June amendment (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001704711/000092189526001629/primary_doc.xml) shows the swap increase. The Q2 10-Q's strategic-alternatives language is a separate document.

findings.finding: Short interest rose to 7.6M shares (about 13.6% of the 56.0M shares outstanding) and 7.6 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement, from 6.7M and 5.2 days at 2026-09-15. That is a crowded short into a print where the company has beaten its own guide twice this year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026 beats (+17.94%, +11.36%) came on similarly short-heavy positioning. In 2025, May 2026 had 4.26M shares short at 6.4 days (equibles).
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is rising into the print rather than being covered, so shorts are positioned for a miss. A squeeze on a beat is the mechanism, and it is not in the price until the number lands. Source is snippet_only (the fetch returned 403).
findings.independence: Fintel shows 12.5% of float short, undated (https://fintel.io/ss/us/fnko). Equibles shows 4.26M at 2026-05-29 (https://equibles.com/stocks/fnko/short-interest), which confirms the build.

findings.finding: Pop Mart's Q3 2026 business update (2026-10-27) had total revenue -45% to -50% YoY and Americas -70% to -75%. This reads ambiguously for Funko. It can mean the US blind-box craze is deflating, which matters because Funko's newest growth driver is POP! Mystery blind boxes. Or it can mean the Labubu competitor that took collectibles share in 2025 is fading.
findings.why_not_priced: Possibly partly priced: FNKO is down ~10% since mid-October, overlapping the Pop Mart update. If fully priced, there would be no further discount, so the size is small. Proxy; neither company has confirmed transmission.
findings.independence: Same figures at https://www.rootdata.com/news/803636. Hasbro and JAKKS (finding 2) point the other way for licensed toys.

findings.finding: Q3 carries no tariff-refund windfall like Q2's $25.4M. Funko sold its $22.1M of IEEPA claims for $19.2M in Q2, and the 10-Q's subsequent-events note says the $6.3M that CBP remitted after quarter-end creates no further gain. Reported Q3 EBITDA ($25-30M guide) will therefore look lower than Q2's $40.9M on a clean basis. Hasbro, by contrast, booked $55M of refunds in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026, which included the $25.4M benefit: +11.36%. The benefit was flagged and the market looked through it to the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Sized at zero because it is guided: the Q3 EBITDA guide already excludes any refund. Filed so a judge does not expect a Hasbro-style refund line.
findings.independence: Shares the 10-Q with finding 4. Hasbro's Q3 refunds are at https://finviz.com/news/404358/hasbro-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results.

findings.finding: Director Charles Denson bought 72,992 shares at $6.85 (~$500k) on 2026-08-24, above today's $6.11. The CEO's sale of 181,893 shares on 2026-09-03 at $5.79 was reported as covering taxes on vesting.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since late August, and the stock is now below the director's price, so its information value is small and only partly reflected.

outside_window.finding: Debt reclassifies to current at 2026-12-31 if refinancing is not completed, and the first net leverage test (max 2.50x) is at the 2026-12-31 quarter end. The Q3 update is in the window (finding 4); the deadline itself is not.

Option chain skew: unusable chain (no two-sided ATM quotes)

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The tape is weak (-8.7% over 5 days) while the evidence leans positive, so the lean cuts against the recent run-down but in the direction a crowded short and two prior beats suggest. The tape weakness and management's Q4 caution hold p_up at 60 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (narrow proxy vs company number): peer read-through finding cut from +1.0 to +0.7, because Funko's own Q2 POS (+6% units) lagged the category series the proxy rests on
Lesson 5/7 (positioning is the information set, and the source is snippet_only): short-interest finding cut from +0.8 to +0.6
Lesson 8 (thin coverage, confirmed company-level beat pattern) and the core's 'guidance change likely': abs_move_pct raised from 14 to 15; p_up left at 60
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the refinancing finding was checked for what the money is for (refinancing paid-down debt at ~2x leverage, not distress), so the small positive stays at +0.3
Lesson 2 (one-offs): the tariff item stays a 0.0 one_off; it has no path to the guide
Lessons 1 and 6 left the guide-beat finding at +2.0: the bar is sourced to the company guide plus three agreeing estimates, and the name has bought its 2026 beats
